_comment: Worked examples, one per module page — the module's idea happening to the orderflow sample project. Inserted after each page's objectives section by domain/insert_figures.py and styled by ../shared/figure (its check.py enforces the closed vocabulary: no inline style, no hex, no links). Symbols, files and counts are real — see labs/sample-project and labs/M01-graph-fundamentals/solution/graph.json. Token counts are illustrative and the figures say so.

M00.title: One question, 147 files or three edges
M00.body:
the question · orderflow
AskedIf I change decode_jwt, what breaks?
explore for it
grep -r decode_jwt → 9 hits open each, follow callers → 147 files read
✗ the window is full, most of it is imports and boilerplate, and the answer is still a guess
ask a graph for it
callers_of(decode_jwt, depth=2) → verify_token → post_invoice → post_payment_webhook
✓ three edges, named, with the file and line each one sits on
Same repository, same question. One reads the codebase to reconstruct a relationship every time it is asked; the other stored the relationship once and looks it up.
M00.caption: Exploration is how an agent discovers structure it has no index for — the cost is not the reading, it is re-deriving the same structure on every question.

M01.title: What a node and an edge actually contain
M01.body:
one node
idclass:services.billing.invoice.Invoice← kind and path, so two Invoices in two services never collide
kindclass
fileservices/billing/invoice.py
line9← what lets an answer be checked instead of believed
one edge
sourcefunction:services.billing.invoice.create_invoice
targetclass:services.billing.invoice.Invoice
typecalls
provenanceEXTRACTED← the parser read this in the source; it is not a deduction
The whole orderflow graph is 36 nodes and 22 edges. Small enough to check by hand, which is exactly why the course uses it — you can verify every answer the graph gives you.
M01.caption: A node without a file and line is trivia; the coordinates are what turn a graph answer into something you can go and read.

M02.title: The chunk that cut the answer in half
M02.body:
chunk 41 of 380 · services/billing/app.py
Containsdef post_invoice(request): ... create_invoice(...)
Does not containthe verify_token call, six lines earlier← the chunk boundary fell between them
retrieved by similarity
Q: does post_invoice check authentication?
▼
No authentication call is visible in this handler.
✗ faithful to the chunk, wrong about the code
answered from edges
calls(post_invoice) → create_invoice → verify_token
✓ the relationship survived, because it was stored as a relationship
M02.caption: Chunking optimises for what text looks similar; a call graph stores what actually reaches what — and those are different questions.

M02B.title: Four levers on one window
M02B.body:
writethe graph itself — structure computed once, read many times
selectcallers_of(decode_jwt) rather than nine grep hits and their files
compressan edge list instead of the function bodies it was derived from
isolatethe parse runs elsewhere; only its conclusion enters the window
without them
147 files ~180,000 tokens one question answered
with them
3 edges + 3 file:line ~400 tokens the same question answered
✓ and the next twenty questions cost the same again
A knowledge graph is not a fifth idea alongside these four. It is what makes all four cheap on a codebase. Counts illustrative.
M02B.caption: The graph is infrastructure for context engineering, not an alternative to it — every lever the discipline names gets easier once structure is stored rather than re-derived.

M03.title: From source text to two edges
M03.body:
services/billing/invoice.py · line 9 onward
Sourceclass Invoice: ...
Sourcedef create_invoice(...): return Invoice(...)
▼
what the parser produced
nodeclass:...invoice.Invoice — file line 9
nodefunction:...invoice.create_invoice
edgecreate_invoice → Invoice · EXTRACTED← the name is right there in the syntax tree
edgecreate_invoice → execute · INFERRED← resolved through an import; a good guess, and labelled as one
Parsing is not the hard part. Deciding which edges you actually saw and which you worked out — and keeping the two apart — is.
M03.caption: Nine of orderflow's 22 edges are EXTRACTED and thirteen INFERRED; a graph that reported all 22 the same way would be twenty-two claims of equal confidence and none of them checkable.

M04.title: The whole repository, in one run
M04.body:
$ graphify labs/sample-project parsed 14 files 36 nodes · 22 edges
provenanceedgeswhat it means for an answer
EXTRACTED9read directly from the syntax tree — quote it
INFERRED13resolved through imports or attributes — check it
AMBIGUOUS0more than one candidate — there were none here
Zero ambiguous edges is a property of a fourteen-file Python service, not of graph building. On a large codebase with dynamic dispatch that column fills up, and the tag is the only thing standing between a plausible answer and a checkable one.
M04.caption: The counts are the artefact: 36 and 22 are small enough to audit by hand, which is the only way to learn to trust a number you will later take on faith at ten thousand.

M05.title: Four tools, one question each answers well
M05.body:
toolbuilt forthe question it answers cheaply
tree-sitterparsingwhat is the structure of this one file?
a language servereditingwhere is this symbol defined, right now, in my editor?
graphifywhole repositorieswhat reaches what, across every file at once?
okf-rsserving knowledgewhat is the canonical description of this concept?
the wrong tool, correctly used
language server: callers of decode_jwt? → accurate, per file, on demand, and only while the editor runs
✗ an agent has no editor session and needs the answer as data
the right one
graph query: callers_of(decode_jwt) → the same answer, as JSON, with provenance on each edge
✓ storable, diffable, servable
M05.caption: None of these tools is wrong; they were built for different consumers, and an agent is a consumer that needs structure as data rather than as a live session.

M06.title: A bundle is a directory you can read without a tool
M06.body:
okf/concepts/authentication.md
frontmatterid: authentication
frontmattersources: [shared/auth.py]← the claim points at what it was derived from
frontmatterupdated: 2026-08-30← the field staleness checks read
bodyEvery request is verified by decode_jwt, which raises AuthError...
knowledge in a database
SELECT body FROM concepts WHERE id = 'authentication'
✗ needs the tool to read it, the tool to diff it, and the tool to review it
knowledge as files
cat okf/concepts/authentication.md git diff okf/
✓ reviewable in a pull request, by a person, with no tool at all
M06.caption: The format's real claim is not expressiveness but reviewability — knowledge that cannot be diffed is knowledge nobody will notice going wrong.

M07.title: The concept file that a directory listing cannot give you
M07.body:
what the code says
shared/auth.py AuthError line 12 decode_jwt line 15 verify_token
All true, all mechanical, and none of it says why.
what the concept file adds
Auth failures raise AuthError rather than returning None, so a half-decoded token can never reach a caller.
✓ the constraint a new caller has to respect, written where it will be read
the boundary worth knowing
Graph can knowwhere WAU is computed, and everything that calls it
Graph cannot knowthat WAU excludes testers on purpose← nothing in the source records the intent, so a human has to
M07.caption: Extraction gets you what the code is; the concept file is where the reasons live — and the reasons are what a new contributor gets wrong.

M08.title: One commit, one file re-parsed
M08.body:
the change
Commitedit services/billing/webhooks.py
Effecthandle_payment_webhook now calls mark_paid
rebuild everything
14 files re-parsed 36 nodes rewritten → every id churns, every downstream diff is noise
✗ correct, and so expensive that it will be run nightly at best
re-parse what changed
1 file re-parsed +1 edge, 0 nodes touched → handle_payment_webhook → mark_paid INFERRED
✓ cheap enough to run on every commit, which is the only cadence that keeps a graph true
A self-updating graph is not a smarter graph. It is a graph whose update is cheap enough that nobody is tempted to skip it.
M08.caption: Freshness is an economics problem before it is an engineering one — the update you run hourly beats the thorough one you run when you remember.

M09.title: The tool returns edges, not files
M09.body:
MCP tool call
Toolcallers_of
Argumentfunction:shared.auth.decode_jwt
a tool that returns source
3 files, 1,240 lines → the agent now has to read them to find the relationship the tool already knew
✗ the graph did the work and then threw the answer away
a tool that returns the answer
verify_token shared/auth.py:31 post_invoice services/billing/app.py post_payment_webhook services/billing/webhooks.py
✓ the shape of the reply is the design decision, not the query
M09.caption: A tool's return value is context you are choosing to spend — returning files hands the model the same reconstruction problem the graph existed to remove.

M10.title: Three stores, three question classes
M10.body:
questionanswered fromwhy not the others
what calls decode_jwt?graphsimilarity cannot follow a call
how do we handle auth failures?concept filethe reason is in no function body
where did we discuss rate limits?vector searchthe wording is fuzzy and the source is prose
one store for everything
embed the whole repo → answers question 3 well → answers question 1 plausibly and wrongly
✗ the failure is silent, because a plausible answer looks like a correct one
routed by question class
classify → graph | concepts | vectors → each question to the store that can actually answer it
✓ and each store stays small, because it holds one kind of thing
M10.caption: Hybrid does not mean querying all three and merging — it means knowing which one owns the question before you ask.

M11.title: Grounded, cited, and out of date
M11.body:
what the graph says
Nodefunction:shared.auth.decode_jwt
Locationshared/auth.py:15
Built8 days ago← the only field that hints anything is wrong
▼
what the file says today
Line 15a docstring — decode_jwt moved to line 34
no staleness gate
answer cites shared/auth.py:15 looks checkable is not checkable
✗ every symptom of a healthy pipeline, because the pipeline is healthy — its input moved
provenance age gate
graph built 8 days ago source changed 2 days ago → FAIL: derived before source
✓ caught in a day, by comparing two timestamps
M11.caption: The dangerous staleness is not the graph that looks broken; it is the one that still answers confidently, with a citation, about a line that has moved.

M12.title: A layout an agent can navigate without being told
M12.body:
structure only a human can hold
src/ utils.py helpers.py main.py stuff/
✗ nothing in the tree says what owns what, so every question starts with exploration
orderflow's shape
services/billing/ services/orders/ services/notifications/ shared/auth.py db.py events.py okf/concepts/
✓ the boundary is in the path, so a graph query can be scoped before it is run
what the layout buys the graph
Scopingcallers_of(publish) within services/notifications
Ownershipshared/ is depended on; services/ depend← a rule the graph can check, not a convention people remember
M12.caption: Project structure is context engineering done before any token is spent: a tree that encodes ownership turns a search into a lookup.

CAPSTONE-2.title: The node that changes what a benchmark means
CAPSTONE-2.body:
the deliberate god node
SymbolRegistry.lookup
Callers1,192← on the full synthetic codebase, and deliberate rather than accidental
blast radius, taken literally
changing Registry.lookup affects 1,192 call sites → "do not touch"
✗ true, useless, and it would say the same about any hub
blast radius, read with judgement
1,192 callers, one contract → the number measures centrality, not risk
✓ the risky change is the one with six callers in three services and no shared contract
A token-reduction benchmark that never meets a node like this reports a saving that will not survive contact with a real repository.
CAPSTONE-2.caption: Centrality is a fact the graph can compute; whether it means danger is a judgement it cannot — and reporting the first as the second is how a metric starts lying.

CAPSTONE.title: The pipeline, end to end, with the gate that makes it trustworthy
CAPSTONE.body:
parse14 files → 36 nodes, 22 edges, each tagged EXTRACTED or INFERRED
enrichconcept files carry the intent the source cannot
serveMCP tools return edges and coordinates, never file dumps
watchany derived file older than its source fails the build
a pipeline that runs
graph built ✓ queries answered ✓ freshness unchecked
✗ works today, and nothing in it will tell you the day it stops being true
a pipeline you can rely on
graph built ✓ queries answered ✓ provenance age gate ✓
✓ the difference is one comparison of two timestamps, run every time
CAPSTONE.caption: Everything before the last row is the part that is fun to build; the last row is the part that decides whether anyone should trust the other three.
